facts.fact: Replit describes General Agent as the most flexible way to work with Replit Agent, with no need to pre-select an artifact type before starting.
facts.quote: General Agent is the most flexible way to work with Replit Agent. You don’t need to pre-select an artifact type or commit to building something specific.

facts.fact: Replit says General Agent can read and write to external services such as BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion, Amplitude, Segment, and Hex, through connectors.
facts.quote: Read and write to external services like BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion, Amplitude, Segment, Hex, and more

facts.fact: According to Replit, users can access General Agent by selecting "General" before writing a prompt on the Replit home page.
facts.quote: Select “General” before writing a prompt on the Replit home page

facts.fact: Replit states that projects imported from GitHub automatically receive General Agent.
facts.quote: Projects imported from GitHub automatically get General Agent

facts.fact: Replit states that General Agent uses progressive disclosure, starting as a lightweight chat and escalating naturally to a full app build.
facts.quote: Start with a lightweight chat and escalate to a full app build naturally

facts.fact: Replit's General Agent transitions from lightweight chat into building an app without requiring the user to start over or switch contexts.
facts.quote: Agent transitions from lightweight chat into building your app seamlessly — no need to start over or switch contexts.

facts.fact: Each General Agent chat is contained within a single Replit project, so the agent cannot see or interact with other projects.
facts.quote: No. Each chat is contained within a single project.

facts.fact: Replit's General Agent cannot access an external tool until the user connects the service through Connectors; once connected, it can read and write to it, but it has no access by default.
facts.quote: You need to connect your services first through Connectors. Once connected, Agent can read and write to them, but it doesn’t have access by default.

facts.fact: Replit states that its currently supported General Agent connectors are BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion, Amplitude, Segment, and Hex, with more being added regularly.
facts.quote: Currently supported: BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion, Amplitude, Segment, Hex, and more.

facts.fact: Replit states that Connectors are optional and General Agent can be used for knowledge work, file generation, and app building without any external connections.
Replit states that General Agent is available to all users, including both Core and Pro plans.
facts.quote: General Agent is available to all users.

facts.fact: Unlike standard Agent with pre-configured environments, Replit's General Agent sets up its own environment and runs commands based on the request, and users may need to ask it to configure publishing before deploying.
facts.quote: You may need to ask it to configure publishing when you’re ready to deploy.

facts.fact: Replit notes that some technologies may not be fully supported in the Nix environment used by General Agent.
facts.quote: Some technologies may not be fully supported in the Nix environment

facts.fact: Replit's General Agent documentation states that connectors are optional and General Agent can be used without any external connections.
facts.quote: No. Connectors are optional. You can use General Agent for knowledge work, file generation, and building apps without any external connections.

facts.fact: Replit's General Agent documentation lists BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion, Amplitude, Segment, and Hex as connectors to connect, plus 'and more'.
facts.value: BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion, Amplitude, Segment, Hex
facts.quote: Connect your services (BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion, Amplitude, Segment, Hex, and more)

facts.fact: Replit's General Agent documentation states that each General Agent chat is contained within a single project, so chats in different projects cannot communicate.
facts.quote: No. Each chat is contained within a single project. You can’t have Project A and Project B talk to each other.

facts.fact: Replit's General Agent documentation states that Agent does not have access to a connected external tool by default and must be connected through Connectors first.
facts.quote: it doesn’t have access by default.

facts.fact: Replit's General Agent documentation states that, unlike standard Agent with pre-configured environments, General Agent sets up its own environment and runs commands based on the user's request.
facts.quote: General Agent sets up its own environment and run commands based on your request.

facts.fact: Replit's General Agent documentation lists Angular, Vue, Svelte, Rust, Go, C#, Python tkinter, Godot games, and CLI tools among frameworks and outputs it can build.
facts.value: Angular, Vue, Svelte, Rust, Go, C#, Python tkinter, Godot games, CLI tools
facts.quote: Angular, Vue, Svelte, Rust, Go, C#, Python tkinter, Godot games, CLI tools, and more
